.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r7/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Known false positives: one criterion covering a whole flow)
evidence: All 26 criteria (2 gates, 16 functional, 6 polish, 4 visual) were compared pairwise. Most are cleanly separated: timer_changes explicitly defers the earlier-versions viewer to edits_and_stale_edit, and wall, client scope, retention, hold, search, order and live-update observables each have one owner. But the functional judge.toml:38 claim 'Each observable is graded in exactly one criterion' is false for the arrival highlight. functional message_links (judge.toml:202) passes only if 'following the link opens M-13 at that message, shown highlighted'. functional/prompt.md says every step must hold and the 'Fails if' line 'never excuses a leg it does not mention'. polish link_highlight (polish/judge.toml:53) grades the same promise from conversations.md:17 ('Opening a message from a link or a search result takes you to it in its thread and highlights it'): 'M-11 opens with that message in view and visibly highlighted ... Fails if nothing sets the message apart'. The same search-result-to-message navigation (search 'Survey booked', open 'Survey booked for Friday.' in M-11) is also graded in functional search_and_transcript Part A (judge.toml:253, 'clicking that result opens M-11 at that message'), which is the prerequisite for link_highlight. That part is a prerequisite overlap and less serious. Minor notes, not blocking: (a) a wrong password being refused appears in the render gate (render/judge.toml:29), in signin_and_client_scope Part A (functional:47-48) and in polish refusal_in_place. The gate makes the functional leg redundant but not contradictory, and refusal_in_place grades the distinct reason-in-place behaviour. (b) Working link previews, mentions and delete are repeated as in-criterion positive controls (wall_mentions_and_links Part A versus message_links; signin_and_client_scope, wall_mentions_and_links and edits_and_stale_edit Part B for the mention list). This follows check 30 and REVIEW_POLICY ('a negative needs a successful control'), so it is not counted as duplication here. No pair demands incompatible products. edits_and_stale_edit leg 4 (transcript shows 'Version two', marked edited) is compatible with search_and_transcript Part B3 (held edited message shows both versions), because they cover different messages and transcripts.md requires both. Source/rubric review only; no judge run exercised this.
counterexample: A conforming-except-highlight app scrolls to the target message on opening a message link or search result, but never highlights it. It loses functional message_links (weight 1.5/44 x 0.6, about 0.020 reward), because 'shown highlighted' is a required pass step. It also loses polish link_highlight (1/6 x 0.2, about 0.033). One missing public promise (conversations.md:17 highlight) is charged twice across dimensions. An app whose search-result click does not navigate fails both search_and_transcript Part A (4.0/44 functional) and link_highlight.
suggested_fix: Remove 'shown highlighted' from message_links. Say 'following the link opens M-13 with that message in view; the highlight itself is graded in polish link_highlight'. Alternatively, make link_highlight the sole owner of highlight across both the link and search routes. Also correct the judge.toml:38 'exactly one criterion' comment if any overlap remains.
